# Door, window and lock electrical faults

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Hold the center console door lock button in LOCK or UNLOCK for more than 5 seconds within 20 seconds of turning ignition on. [t936]

[Partial] Identify auto-locking behavior and determine if it occurs at 15 mph. [t936]

[Partial] Replace the airbag light's old LED with a new 3mm unit and reset the electrical faults. [t764]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Turn the key to the ON position.
2. Wait for the airbag light to illuminate and then turn the key OFF immediately.
3. [Partial] Wait five seconds before turning the key back to ON.
4. [Partial] Repeat the previous two steps twice more.
5. Turn the key on again until the airbag light begins flashing slowly.
6. [Partial] Wait ten or more seconds, then turn the key OFF.
7. [Partial] Wait another ten seconds and start the truck.
8. Remove the center dash plastic cover for the HVAC and radio.
9. Unscrew the airbag light from the plastic dash cover using a Torx screwdriver or small flathead.
10. Snip off two or three of the plastic caps holding the circuit board in place with wire cutters.
11. Fold one intact cap's circuit board part to separate it from the main piece.
12. [Partial] Heat each side of the old LED and push until it slides off without damaging the board.
13. Solder a new 3mm LED onto the positive pad, holding it down before bending it upward.
14. [Partial] Assemble all parts in reverse order starting with the circuit board.
15. Apply a drop of super glue at the edge where you snipped the plastic tabs.

_Procedure reported by [t764]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-change-color-of-passenger-airbag-light-led-05-08.8918/>_

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t936] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Close all doors until the door switches turn off.
2. Turn the ignition switch on.
3. [Partial] Hold the center console door lock button in the LOCK position for more than 5 seconds within 20 seconds of turning the ignition on.
4. Wait for the hazard lamps to blink twice to confirm the setting changed from OFF to ON.
5. [Partial] Close all doors until the door switches turn off again.
6. Turn the ignition switch on once more.
7. [Partial] Hold the center console door lock button in the UNLOCK position for more than 5 seconds within 20 seconds of turning the ignition on.
8. Wait for the hazard lamps to blink once to confirm the setting changed from ON to OFF.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t936] [Partial]</summary>

1. Identify the specific auto-locking behavior you want to control.
2. Determine if the issue is locking at 15 mph or unlocking when removing the key.

</details>

## Tools

- Philips screwdriver [t764]
- Wire cutters or similar tool [t764]

## Specifications

- **LED size**: 3mm [t764] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Wait time after first cycle**: 5 Seconds [t764] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- The hazard lamps blinking confirms the switching is complete. [t936]
- One blink indicates a change from ON to OFF, while two blinks indicate OFF to ON. [t936]
- Set both modes to 'off' to convert power locks into manual operation. [t936]
- Use a small flathead screwdriver if the specific Torx bit is unavailable. [t764]
- Apply super glue at the edge of the circuit board where plastic tabs were snipped to secure it. [t764]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Removing the LED without replacing or soldering it securely, causing the light to illuminate and requiring a reset procedure. [t764]
- [Partial] Messing up the solid solder connection on the positive pad so the system detects an open circuit. [t764]
